children: US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in roughly $2 billion in net inflows over the past week, marking the most aggressive institutional buying spree since late 2025. The catch: Bitcoin itself briefly kissed $87,397, then promptly got rejected and slid back below $84,000.

The week's standout moment came on September 21, when spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a single-day net inflow of approximately $999 million. That figure represents the largest one-day haul since October 2025, back when Bitcoin was riding very different momentum.

The buying didn't stop there. September 22 brought in another $715 million, followed by $347 million on September 23. Three consecutive days of heavy accumulation that, in aggregate, pushed the week's total past the $2 billion mark.

Breaking down that record September 21 session reveals the usual suspects leading the charge. BlackRock's IBIT absorbed $381 million, ARK 21Shares' ARKB took in $289 million, and Fidelity's FBTC attracted $239 million. Together, those three products accounted for the vast majority of the day's inflows, reinforcing just how concentrated the ETF market remains among a handful of heavyweight issuers.

Since August 19, cumulative ETF net inflows have reached approximately $4.6 billion. More importantly, that sustained buying has dragged 2026 year-to-date flows into positive territory at roughly +$320 million. That's a notable turnaround after what was a bruising stretch of outflows earlier in the year.

Bitcoin's price briefly surpassed $87,000 for the first time since January, hitting an intraday high of $87,397. The price quickly retreated below $84,000, establishing $87K as a formidable resistance level.

The rally itself was partly fueled by short liquidations, a familiar dynamic where rising prices force bearish traders to close their positions, which in turn accelerates the move higher. When the reversal hit, it triggered long liquidations in the other direction. Analysts have identified support levels between $82,000 and $85,000 as the range to watch for signs of whether this pullback is a healthy pause or something more concerning.

Year-to-date ETF flows flipping positive after months of net outflows suggests institutional sentiment toward Bitcoin is genuinely shifting. Earlier in 2026, spot Bitcoin ETFs were bleeding capital as macro uncertainty and a prolonged price drawdown tested conviction. Cumulative flows since mid-August alone total $4.6 billion.

BlackRock, Fidelity, and ARK 21Shares dominating the inflow leaderboard also matters. When IBIT alone absorbs $381 million in a single session, it reflects the kind of institutional plumbing that pension funds, endowments, and registered investment advisors actually use.

A gap is forming between ETF demand and price action. Two billion dollars in weekly buying should, in theory, provide meaningful upward pressure. The fact that Bitcoin couldn't hold $87K despite that level of accumulation suggests sellers are equally motivated at these prices. The key question for the coming weeks is whether this pace of inflows can sustain itself, or whether that $82,000 to $85,000 support zone will get tested quickly.

title: Bitcoin ETFs accumulate $2B this week amid price rejection at $87K
